title: Where Does the Bullet's Energy Go?

props.footnote: Arrow widths are illustrative, not measured

props.question: Find the kinetic energy of a 10 g bullet moving at 400 m/s.
The bullet stops in 8 cm of wood. Find the average force the wood exerts.
Find the speed of the block (with the bullet) just after impact.

items.right: Energy is conserved, it is dissipated to the surroundings
E_k = ½ m v^2: square the speed
Momentum is conserved; E_k is not (inelastic)

questions.text: A bullet is fired from a gun into a wooden block, where it stops. Describe the energy transfers from firing to stopping.
A 15 g bullet at 350 m/s stops in 0.12 m of wood. Calculate (a) its kinetic energy (b) the average resistive force.
A bullet embeds in a block on a smooth surface. Explain why momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not.
